hypotheses.justification: This follows from `hq_pos` and `hq_bound`. Casting gives 1 ≤ (q:ℝ) < (n:ℝ)/2, so (n:ℝ) > 2. Since n is a natural number, n ≥ 3 ≥ 2. A proof without `hn` first derives `have hn : 2 ≤ n` from these two facts (cast `hq_pos` to ℝ, combine with `hq_bound`, then `exact_mod_cast` / `linarith`), and then runs the existing proof unchanged: `error_split_bound n hn …` and `combine_error_P0_Palpha n hn`. Deleting this one hypothesis alone works. `hq_bound` can also be deleted (see the other entry); dropping both together still works, using the case split described there.

This is unnecessary because when it fails the conclusion holds trivially. Split on whether (q:ℝ) < n/2. If it holds, use the existing proof. Otherwise q ≥ n/2: take B = ∅. Then `B.card = 0 ≤ …` holds in ℕ. The ∀-clause is vacuous: from `1 ≤ p` and `(p:ℝ) + q < n/2 ≤ q` we get (p:ℝ) < 0, which contradicts p ≥ 1 (by `linarith` after casting `hp_pos`). So the statement stays true and provable without `hq_bound`, with or without `hn` (in the case q < n/2, `hn` can be recovered as in the other entry).
